provenance.definition: Derived from the Math Art generator registries and cross-referenced to the literature; not transcribed from any gallery's compilation.
sources: David Swart, "Arcs on Spheres and Snakes on Planes", Bridges 2024 (the sphericon = solid of revolution of a regular polygon, halved and its cross-section rotated onto itself).
I. Sabitov / P. Roberts (polysphericons); H-ITS Polysphericons project, https://www.h-its.org/projects/polysphericons/ .
Sphericon invented by Colin J. Roberts (Baldock, England); popularized by Ian Stewart, "Cone with a Twist", Mathematical
Recreations, Scientific American, October 1999.  See also Wikipedia "sphericon".
